commitResults.messageTitle: Update UG and DG for delete by UUID
commitResults.messageBody:
Document the UUID-based delete syntax, example and error cases in the UG,
and update the DG command description, use case UC3, manual testing steps
and the affected sequence/state diagrams. Remove references to deleting
by index.

Fixes #71
Add delete by short UUID

Update UG and DG for delete by UUID

A hand-edited or corrupted data file can contain a uuid that is not a
valid UUID. UUID.fromString then throws an unchecked
IllegalArgumentException, which escapes the usual IllegalValueException
handling for invalid fields. It also silently accepts shortened forms
such as "1-1-1-1-1".

Check the stored uuid against the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form
and throw IllegalValueException when it does not match, so a bad uuid
is reported like any other invalid field.

Log when a legacy save without a uuid is given a fresh one.

The short UUID length of 7 is hard-coded in three places: the
substring in Person#getShortUuid, the delete parser's regex and the
delete usage message. Changing the length means finding and updating
every copy, and missing one makes the card and the parser disagree.

Define the length once as Person.SHORT_UUID_LENGTH and use it
everywhere.

commitResults.messageTitle: Gradle: Add JUnit parameterized tests dependency
commitResults.messageBody:
Tests that run the same check over many inputs are currently written
as near-identical copies, one per input, which the code quality
guidelines flag as duplication.

Add junit-jupiter-params so such tests can use @ParameterizedTest.

Two persons can share the 7-character short UUID shown on their
cards. The delete command then asks for a more specific identifier,
but it accepts exactly 7 characters, so neither person can be
deleted. The error also does not show the user what to type.

Accept any UUID prefix from 7 to 32 hexadecimal characters, ignoring
dashes, so that a full UUID copied from the data file also works.
When several persons match, list each one's full UUID and name so
the user can see how many characters tell them apart.

Move prefix matching into Person#hasUuidPrefix, and split the lookup
in DeleteCommand into its own method with logging and an assertion.
Use parameterized tests and shared helpers in the delete tests to
remove near-duplicate test cases.

JsonAdaptedPersonTest checks that a malformed uuid is rejected, but
nothing checks that the rejection reaches the storage layer as a
DataLoadingException, which is what lets the app start with an empty
address book instead of crashing.

Add a data file with a malformed uuid and check that reading it
throws DataLoadingException.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add undelete command to restore deleted persons
commitResults.messageBody:
A deleted person is gone for good, so an agent who deletes the wrong
client by mistake has to re-enter every detail by hand, and the
client gets a new UUID.

Add an undelete command that restores the most recently deleted
person, keeping their UUID, at the position they were deleted from.
Repeating it walks further back through this session's deletes.

The model keeps the deleted persons and their indexes in a stack for
the session only. Undelete refuses to restore a person who already
exists, e.g. after being re-added by hand, and keeps them on the
stack so nothing is lost. It takes no arguments, and rejects any, so
it cannot be mistaken for a delete.

commitResults.messageTitle: UndeleteCommand: Explain how to undelete over a same-name person
commitResults.messageBody:
If a person with the same name is added after a delete, undelete
refuses to restore the deleted person, as names must be unique. The
error says a person "identical to" the deleted one exists, which is
wrong when the new person only shares the name, and it does not tell
the user how to get the deleted person back.

Keep the refusal, as restoring would leave two persons with one name
and replacing the newer person would silently lose their data. Change
the message to say the names clash and to rename that person with edit
before running undelete again.

Add tests that a different person with the same name blocks undelete,
and that renaming them lets the deleted person be restored.

Contact field validation currently rejects useful descriptive values such as parenthesized names, labeled phone numbers, and multiple email addresses.

Allow these descriptions while retaining validation for empty, malformed, and unsupported values, and document the accepted formats in command help and the User Guide.

Names currently reject slash notation such as s/o and d/o even though these forms are common in contact names.

Allow slashes in names, document parser ambiguity for field-like prefixes, and cover s/o and d/o inputs with tests.

Users can enter names that closely resemble existing entries without feedback, making accidental typos easy to miss.

Add normalized Levenshtein matching to add and edit flows, preserve duplicate handling, and document that warnings are advisory while covering edge cases with tests.
Allow More Flexible Descriptions in Add Command

Add command errors currently do not consistently identify the failing field, and missing-information guidance appears after the full usage text.

Report field-specific errors, position the UNKNOWN hint with the parameter format, and remove outdated punctuation restrictions from add guidance.

Add command executions currently have no command-specific outcome logs.

Log duplicate rejections and successful additions so command outcomes can be diagnosed without recording contact details.

Permit punctuation in names, phone numbers, emails, and addresses while retaining validation for blank values, control characters, length limits, and field semantics. Report add-command errors by field and provide UNKNOWN guidance for missing information.

commitResults.messageTitle: Prioritize UUID display in person cards
commitResults.messageBody: Keep UUID labels at their preferred width so they remain fully visible when names are long. Allow person-card fields to wrap and expose complete values through wrapped tooltips.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update edit command targeting and remarks
commitResults.messageBody: Use short UUIDs to identify people consistently with the remark command and allow edit to update or clear remarks. Replace generic edit target errors with actionable UUID guidance and document the revised syntax.

Flatten quoted-value unescaping with early continuation and isolate escaped-character handling in a helper. Preserve supported and unsupported escape sequences while making the control flow easier to follow.

Allow add to accept an optional r/REMARK field while preserving the empty default when omitted. Keep validation hints concise and explain the email @ requirement, with parser and guide coverage for the new syntax.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support dashed UUID prefixes in edit command
commitResults.messageBody: Edit currently accepts only seven-character UUID prefixes, which prevents users from using longer prefixes or full UUIDs copied from the data file.\n\nNormalize dashes and case before validating edit targets, and accept prefixes from seven to 32 hexadecimal characters.

The edit UUID validation and remark-aware descriptor equality paths lack direct tests, leaving recently changed behavior less protected.\n\nAdd invalid UUID constructor cases and a descriptor equality case with differing remarks to exercise these paths.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow duplicate UNKNOWN names in add
commitResults.messageBody: The add command currently rejects all duplicate names, including entries whose name is unknown.\n\nAllow exact uppercase UNKNOWN names to be added repeatedly, retain normal duplicate checks for other names, and document the exception with test coverage.
Add command is too restrictive

The default build now produces ClientConnect.jar, but the user guide still instructs users to launch addressbook.jar.\n\nDocument the current ClientConnect.jar filename so the launch instructions match the build output.
Updating default build name
Adding logger to Add command

commitResults.messageTitle: Scope quoted argument handling to field parsers
commitResults.messageBody: Global quote handling causes literal punctuation in remark and find arguments to be rejected or altered.\n\nKeep the default tokenizer literal, enable quoted-value parsing only for add and edit, and add regression and field-validation coverage for the review findings.

Combine upstream documentation, help, logging, and UNKNOWN-name behavior with punctuation-aware add parsing and remark support. Preserve field-specific validation messages and empty-field guidance while integrating the latest upstream tests and assets.
Add command could support punctuation in all fields
